data.one_liner: Run Dart isolates in Flutter that can interact with Flutter plugins.
data.what_it_does: Allows you to spawn and manage Dart isolates in Flutter that have access to platform plugins. It provides APIs similar to standard isolates along with `flutterCompute` to execute expensive tasks off the main thread.
use_when: You need to run long-running or CPU-intensive background tasks that must interact with Flutter plugins
You want to offload work from the main UI thread on Android and iOS
avoid_when: Standard Dart isolates or Flutter's built-in compute function are sufficient and plugin access inside the isolate is not required
You want automatic event loop termination when work completes (FlutterIsolates require explicit termination)
strengths: Enables plugin usage inside spawned background isolates
Supports custom plugin registrants for both iOS and Android
Provides a simple `flutterCompute` wrapper for single tasks
weaknesses: Event loop will not terminate automatically, requiring explicit `kill()` calls
Has not been tested with a wide range of plugins
Entrypoints require specific `@pragma('vm:entry-point')` annotations to prevent release mode crashes
data.setup_notes: Entrypoint functions must be top-level or static and decorated with @pragma('vm:entry-point'). Custom plugin registrants may need platform-specific configuration in Swift or Java.
